units.title: Curvature controls the interpolation derivative expression
units.statement: Let L be a real-linear generator and suppose it satisfies CD(α,∞): αΓ(f)≤Γ₂(f). Expanding Γ₂ gives the pointwise lower bound LΓ(f)−2Γ(f,Lf)≥2αΓ(f).
assumptions: The state space X is arbitrary.
L is a real-linear map from real-valued observables on X to real-valued observables on X.
The curvature parameter α is strictly positive.
For every observable g and point y, the exact expanded inequality αΓ(g,g)(y)≤(1/2)(LΓ(g,g)(y)−Γ(g,Lg)(y)−Γ(g,Lg)(y)) holds.
No semigroup or differentiability assumption is present.

steps.title: Specialize the expanded curvature premise
steps.text: At the chosen observable and point, the globally quantified hypothesis gives the exact one-half normalized inequality.
steps.lean: Specialize hcurvature to f and x.

steps.title: Combine the repeated mixed terms
steps.text: The two identical subtractions are exactly twice the mixed carré-du-champ term.
steps.lean: Real-ring normalization identifies the repeated terms.

steps.title: Clear the factor one half
steps.text: Multiply the specialized inequality by two and normalize the real arithmetic.
steps.lean: nlinarith closes the scalar real inequality.

units.lean_statement: Lean exposes the arbitrary type X, linear generator, α>0, every curvature quantifier, the one-half normalization, the observable f, and the point x directly in the theorem signature.
units.lean_proof: The proof specializes the fully expanded curvature hypothesis and discharges the exact real-arithmetic consequence; no hidden definition is unfolded.
units.boundary: This is the algebraic curvature-to-derivative-expression step only. It does not construct a Markov semigroup, prove order preservation, establish the identity d/ds[P_s Γ(P_{t-s}f)]=2P_s Γ₂(P_{t-s}f), or justify generator-domain closure.
